description: A team of Computer Science undergraduate students from AWH Engineering College, Kozhikode, collaborating to build practical software solutions for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, space-themed web application built with HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript to address the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Designed as a browser-based training simulator for aspiring young explorers, the module guides users through four critical spaceflight scenarios: International Space Station (ISS) solar array maintenance, habitat pressure leak diagnostics, microgravity physics, and orbital mechanics. Each module presents realistic operational problems, delivers immediate educational feedback, and concludes with a mission readiness debrief score. By translating complex aerospace engineering and orbital physics principles into accessible, hands-on decision-making exercises, this trainer lowers the barrier to STEM education and inspires students to understand how real astronauts prepare for deep-space missions.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based simulation game built using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, designed to train aspiring young astronauts through gamified spaceflight challenges.

​How it works: The application features multiple educational modules tackling real mission scenarios, including International Space Station (ISS) solar array maintenance, habitat pressure leak diagnostics, microgravity physics, and orbital mechanics. Users make choices through an intuitive graphical interface, receiving immediate feedback and a final mission readiness score debrief.

​Benefits & Impact: It lowers the barrier to entry for aerospace education, making complex STEM concepts engaging, accessible, and fun for students and young learners.

​Tools used: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Google Slides (for presentation demonstration), and VS Code.
